interpretation: Instruction: 'Put the bowl on the plate'. Robot: capx_libero_panda (7-DOF Panda, parallel-jaw gripper, stroke 0.08 m, max_width 0.079 m, closed_empty 0.985, held_below 0.95; cameras 'agentview' (scene, facing the robot) and 'robot0_eye_in_hand' (wrist)). The bowl is the only bowl in the scene: obj20, a grey bowl with a black-and-white floral pattern inside and a yellow rim, 11x11x5 cm. A rim circle fit put it at (0.6025, 0.1202), rim radius 0.054 m, rim top z 0.040, sitting on the table (z -0.012). The plate is obj12, a flat white plate with red rings, 14x14x2 cm, centre (0.4577, -0.0453), centre surface z about -0.005. Goal: the bowl resting upright on the plate, ideally centred, with nothing else disturbed. Nothing was ambiguous. The bowl is wider (11 cm) than the gripper's 7.9 cm maximum, so it cannot be gripped across its diameter and has to be pinched at the rim.
plan: Pinch the bowl wall top-down from the +y side of the rim, where nothing stands beyond it. The -x side was rejected because the outer finger would come down 3.7 cm from the stove's edge. The TCP goes over the rim at radius 0.050 from the bowl centre, fingers closing radially along world y (top_down yaw -90, the same orientation as home, so no wrist rotation). The TCP is lowered to z 0.036 so the fingertips (about 0.015 m below the TCP, from the FK 'finger_joint_tip' sites) are about 2 cm below the rim. Close, lift 10 cm, then check from the point cloud where the bowl sits relative to the TCP. Then carry it level so the bowl centre lands over the plate centre, lower it until its bottom is about 5 mm above the plate surface, open, and retract straight up. The only change along the way came from the harness's tight joint-speed limit: the first 3 s approach was refused (min_duration 10.2 s), so every motion was re-timed to the previewed minimum plus margin (12.5 s approach, 4 s lift, 14 s transport). Steps were never a constraint.

steps.what: Read the embodiment, observe(), objects(), and agentview, wrist and annotated images
steps.why: Identify the robot, the bowl and the plate
steps.result: Bowl = obj20 at (0.603, 0.120), plate = obj12 at (0.458, -0.045). Other objects: stove obj6/obj1, cream cheese obj19, wine bottle obj24, cabinet obj21, wine rack (several brown ids). Step 0.

steps.what: Measured the bowl from object_points and the fused cloud: rim circle fit, radial height profile, outer-wall profile; plate surface heights; FK link poses and finger collision spheres
steps.why: Choose a rim pinch that fits the 7.9 cm gripper and set the grasp depth
steps.result: Rim centre (0.6025, 0.1202), r 0.054, top z 0.040. The wall flares from r about 0.045 at z 0.01 to 0.056 at the rim and is about 4-5 mm thick. Fingertips are about 0.015 m below the TCP. Plate centre surface z about -0.005.

steps.what: Previewed approach variants (direct; rotate about the base first; lower first; via a midpoint)
steps.why: The 3 s direct approach was refused as too fast (needed at least 10.2 s), with a warning that joint 2 passes near 0
steps.result: Direct at 12.5 s was ok. Joint trajectory smooth (at most 0.005 rad per step, q1 and q3 nearly constant), arm collision-free under check_batch.

steps.what: Executed the approach to the pre-grasp at TCP (0.6025, 0.1702, 0.12), gripper open
steps.result: Done, 256 steps (step 256). The rim circle projected into the wrist image matched the real rim. The planned TCP was on the rim, the inner fingertip inside the bowl and the outer one outside.

steps.what: Descended to TCP z 0.036 in 3 s
steps.why: Straddle the bowl wall with the open fingers
steps.result: Done (step 322). Agentview showed one finger inside the bowl near its centre and one outside the +y rim. The wrist view showed the rim between the fingers.
Reading 0.921, gap 6.4 mm, below held_below 0.95, so held. The wrist image showed the fingers closed on the rim and the bowl barely moved (step 352).

steps.what: Lifted 10 cm in 4 s (3 s was 1.01x too fast)
steps.why: Raise the bowl clear of the table and confirm the grip
steps.result: Bowl hanging level in the air in agentview; reading 0.929. A wrist-camera rim fit put the bowl centre at (0.602, 0.1185) and its bottom about 0.048 below the TCP, so the TCP-to-bowl offset is (-0.0005, -0.0515). Rim radius unchanged, so no tilt (step 438).

steps.what: Transport plus descent in one 14 s preview: above the place point at z 0.136, then TCP (0.4582, 0.0062, 0.050)
steps.why: Put the bowl centre over the plate centre with its bottom about 5 mm above the plate
steps.result: Arm collision-free; executed, 286 steps (step 724). The bowl was over the plate in both cameras. A rim fit put the bowl centre at about (0.461, -0.042), within 4 mm of the plate centre. The gripper reading drifted to 0.957 (gap 3.4 mm) but the wrist view still showed the fingers pinching the rim.

steps.why: Release the bowl onto the plate
steps.result: Gap 0.079. The bowl settled in the plate; the inner finger was left inside the bowl near its centre (step 754).

steps.what: Retracted straight up 11 cm in 5 s
steps.why: Clear the gripper without touching the bowl

steps.what: Final check: fresh agentview and wrist images, reperceive, rim circle fit, rim height per quadrant
steps.result: The bowl stands upright on the plate. Its rim centre (0.4601, -0.0388) is 2.4 mm / 6.5 mm from the plate centre. Rim top z about 0.045-0.0495, so it rests on the plate surface. Rim heights are within about 2 mm across quadrants, so it is level. Cream cheese, bottle, stove and cabinet are untouched. Called finish_episode at step 860 of 7990.

key_images.caption: Start (agentview): bowl to the right of the cream cheese, plate to the left of it, stove at the back right
Perception ids: bowl obj20, plate obj12, cream cheese obj19, bottle obj24, stove obj6/obj1, cabinet obj21
Wrist view at the pre-grasp: the fitted rim circle (yellow) matches the real rim; planned TCP on the +y rim with the inner and outer fingertip positions
At grasp height: one finger inside the bowl, one outside the +y rim
After closing: fingers pinch the bowl rim (reading 0.921, held)
Bowl lifted 10 cm, hanging level from the rim pinch
Bowl lowered over the plate centre, just above the plate surface, before release
Gripper opened: bowl resting in the plate
Final (agentview): bowl upright and centred on the plate, gripper retracted, other objects undisturbed
Final (wrist, from above): bowl centred inside the plate's rim

lessons: 1) LIBERO bowls (about 11 cm) are wider than the Panda's 7.9 cm opening. A top-down rim pinch works: TCP at about rim radius minus 4 mm, fingers closing radially, fingertips about 2 cm below the rim. The hold read about 0.92-0.93 on the 4-5 mm wall, and the bowl hung level because its centre of mass sits along the closing axis. 2) In this harness, joint speed limits are tight: plan about 12 s for a 25 cm reach from home and about 4 s per 10 cm vertical move, and take the preview's min_duration instead of guessing. 3) Project the fitted rim circle and the planned fingertip points into the wrist image before descending; it is a cheap, convincing alignment check. 4) A held object drops out of objects(). Get its pose from wrist-camera cloud points in a z band, leaving out points near the fingers, then fit a circle; that gave a TCP-to-bowl offset accurate to a few mm for the placement. 5) The gripper reading can drift past held_below while still holding (0.929 to 0.957 here); check the wrist image instead of trusting the threshold alone.
